decisive_items: papules and pustules on an erythematous base over the nasal dorsum
treated with systemic and topical antibiotics at a local hospital without improvement
response.rationale: R1 best fits the nasal papulopustular eruption with ulceration/crusting and antibiotic failure, typical of facial granulomatous dermatitis. R4 (rosacea) is plausible but usually responds to antibiotics and lacks ulceration; R2 (pyoderma gangrenosum) typically painful and lower-extremity; R3 and R5 are less specific.

rejected.why: Pyoderma gangrenosum usually presents with painful, rapidly progressive ulcers, often on legs, and is associated with systemic disease; here no pain or systemic features.
Folliculitis typically responds to antibiotics and lacks ulceration/crusting.
Rosacea may show papules/pustules but usually has flushing and responds to antibiotics; ulceration is atypical.
Sarcoidosis skin lesions are usually papules/plaques without pustules or crusting, and systemic symptoms are often present.
